title: Constructing a nuanced argument / Nkwado okwu n'okpuru n'okpuru nke dị mma na ndoro ndoro
bridge: Na English, nkwado okwu n'okpuru n'okpuru nke dị mma na ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na adverbs nke ndoro (e.g., 'somewhat', 'arguably'), modals nke ndoro (e.g., 'might', 'could'), na nkọwa ndoro (e.g., 'although', 'while'). N'okpuru Spanish, ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na subjunctives (n'ihi na, n'ihi na, n'ihi na), English na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na ndoro ndoro. N'ihi na ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na ndoro ndoro, n'ihi na English na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma. N'ihi na ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na ndoro ndoro, n'ihi na English na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma.
rule: Iji nkwado okwu n'okpuru n'okpuru nke dị mma na English na level C1, hụ na: 1) Adverbs nke ndoro (e.g., 'arguably', 'apparently', 'probably') iji kpọtụrụ ndoro ndoro nke onye na-eme ka okwu. 2) Modals nke ndoro (might, may, could) iji kpọtụrụ ndoro ndoro nke ndoro. 3) Connectors nke ndoro (although, even though, while, whereas) iji nkwado okwu n'okpuru n'okpuru. 4) Structures nke dị ka 'it could be argued that...', 'one might say that...', 'this is not to say that...' iji nkwado okwu n'okpuru n'okpuru. Hụ na ndoro ndoro nke okwu: na English, ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma, mana ọ bụghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma. Hụ na ndoro ndoro nke 'maybe' (informal) na contexts nke dị mma; hụ na 'perhaps' ma ọ bụ 'possibly'.

common_error.explanation: Na Spanish, ọ bụrụ na ndoro ndoro na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na 'aunque... pero' iji nkwado ndoro ndoro, mana na English, ọ bụghị iji hụ 'although' na 'but' nwere ọnụ. Hụ na ụzọ ọ bụla. Ma 'aunque' na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na 'although'/'though' n'ime ndoro, na 'but' na-enyeghị n'ụzọ dịrị mma na ndoro ndoro n'ime ndoro ndoro.

title: Critical Analysis and Evaluation / Ntuzu okpuru na nkà
bridge: Na Spanish, anyị na-egosi nkà n'okpuru ndoro ndoro na usoro dị ka 'eme ka', 'ọ dị mma ịtụle ya' ma ọ bụ okpuru subjuntivo. Na English, ị ga-eme ka ị nwere ike ịmụta okpuru modals (may, might, could) iji mee ka ọ dị mma, adverbs nke ndoro (highly, somewhat, arguably) na usoro ndoro ndoro (It is worth noting). Ọ bụrụ na ndoro nke a na-eme banyere 'must' na okpuru niile na Spanish bụ 'debe ser', n'ihi na na English, 'must' na-eme ka ọ dị mma nke ndoro ndoro, a na-eme ka ọ dị mma nke ndoro. Nke a na-eme ka ị ga-eme ka ị nwere ike ịmụta okpuru modals na adverbs nke ndoro ndoro iji mee ka ọ dị mma. Na English, ị na-eme ka ọ dị mma na ndoro ndoro na ndoro ndoro na ndoro ndoro.
rule: Iji nkà n'okpuru na English na C1 level, bido: 1) Okpuru modals iji mee ka ọ dị mma nke ndoro: 'must' (ndoro ndoro), 'may/might/could' (ndoro), 'can't' (ndoro ndoro). 2) Adverbs nke ndoro: 'highly', 'extremely', 'somewhat', 'arguably', 'undoubtedly'. 3) Usoro ndoro ndoro: 'It is worth noting that...', 'It could be argued that...', 'The evidence suggests...'. 4) Okpuru ndoro: 'I would argue', 'I contend', 'I maintain' (ndoro ndoro na 'I think'). 5) Connectors nke ndoro ndoro: 'however', 'nevertheless', 'whereas'. Gbalịa ịgụ 'I think' na ndoro ndoro na ndoro ndoro; bido 'This implies that...' ma ọ bụ 'It could be inferred that...'. Iji nkà, bido 'strengths and weaknesses', 'implications', 'limitations'.

Na English ndoro ndoro, ị ga-eme ka ị nwere ike ịmụta okpuru modals na adverbs nke ndoro ndoro iji mee ka ọ dị mma, ma ị gbalịa ịgụ 'I think' na ndoro ndoro akademikị. title: Irony and Understatement / Ironía, sarcasmo na eufemismo
bridge: NꞌIgbo, ironía, sarcasmo na eufemismo na-akwado na ntughari na mkpuruokwu ndoro ndoro (dị ka 'ndoro', 'nke a ga-eme', 'banyere a'), ma na-akwado na-eme ntinye ma obiara na-eme nnyocha. NꞌEnglish, ironía na-achọpụta na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ, na eufemismo bụ ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro. Nke a bụ ọtụtụ: nꞌEnglish, understatement bụ ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro (dị ka 'not bad' tụọrọ 'mma'). NꞌIgbo, ndị a na-achọta na-eme nnyocha ma na-eme nnyocha ma na-eme nnyocha. Ma ọ bụrụ na ị na-akwado ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro, ị nwere ike ịmalite ịnweta ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.
rule: NꞌEnglish na level C1, ironía na eufemismo na-achọpụta na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ: 1) Understatement: na-akwado adịective ma ọ bụ adverbị nke na-akwado nke na-akwado nke na-akwado nke na-akwado nke (dị ka 'It's not the worst idea' tụọrọ 'ọ bụrụ na ọ dị mma'; 'a bit' ma ọ bụ 'slightly' tụọrọ nke na-akwado nke na-akwado nke na-akwado). 2) Sarcasmo: na-akwado na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ (na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ). 3) Eufemismo: na-akwado mkpuruokwu ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro (dị ka 'passed away' tụọrọ 'were', 'let go' tụọrọ 'were fired', 'between jobs' tụọrọ 'were unemployed', 'full-figured' tụọrọ 'were fat'). Ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro: adverbs nke na-akwado nke na-akwado nke na-akwado nke na-akwado nke (dị ka 'hardly', 'barely', 'scarcely') tụọrọ understatement; nkọwa ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro (dị ka 'Is that so?') tụọrọ ironía; ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'just', 'only', 'a bit' tụọrọ ndoro ndoro ndoro. concept_examples.text: That's a bit of an exaggeration, don't you think?
concept_examples.translation: A na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a?
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðæts ə bɪt əv ən ɪɡˌzædʒəˈreɪʃən, doʊnt juː θɪŋk/

concept_examples.text: The weather is not exactly tropical here.
concept_examples.translation: Akwụkwọ ndụ a adịghị mma nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈweðər ɪz nɒt ɪɡˈzæktli ˈtrɒpɪkəl hɪər/

concept_examples.text: He's been known to stretch the truth occasionally.
concept_examples.translation: Ọmụmaatụ, ọ bụrụ na ọ na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a.
concept_examples.phonetic: /hiːz biːn noʊn tə strɛtʃ ðə truːθ əˈkeɪʒənəli/

concept_examples.translation: Nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a! (ironía)

common_error.wrong: No está mal, ¿eh? (como respuesta a algo excelente, literal translation)
common_error.explanation: Error a na-eme nꞌịtụgharị 'not bad' dị ka 'a na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a'. NꞌIgbo, 'not bad' dị ka 'a na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a' tụọrọ 'mma'. Ma nꞌEnglish, 'not bad' tụọrọ 'a na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a' tụọrọ 'mma'. Ma nꞌEnglish, tụọrọ 'not half bad' tụọrọ 'mma'. Ma ọ bụrụ na ị na-akwado ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro, tụọrọ 'mma' tụọrọ 'mma'.

levels.label: Understatement with adverbs of degree
levels.translation: Understatement na-adịbe adverbs nke na-akwado nke

examples.original: I'm a bit confused about the instructions.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm ə bɪt kənˈfjuːzd əˈbaʊt ði ɪnˈstrʌkʃənz/
examples.translation: Am a na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a n'okwu ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Nꞌebe a, 'a bit' na-akwado nke a bụ nke a tụọrọ 'were confused', ma nꞌebe ọzọ, ọ bụrụ na ọ na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a.

examples.original: It's a bit chilly today, isn't it? (said in a blizzard)
examples.phonetic: /ɪts ə bɪt ˈtʃɪli təˈdeɪ, ˈɪzənt ɪt/
examples.translation: Ezigbo a na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a n'okwu ndoro ndoro n'okwu ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Nꞌokwu ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro 'a bit' tụọrọ nke a bụ nke a tụọrọ nke a bụ nke a.

examples.original: She's not exactly the most organized person.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiːz nɒt ɪɡˈzæktli ðə moʊst ˈɔːrɡənaɪzd ˈpɜːrsən/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a n'okwu ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: 'Not exactly' bụ ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro tụọrọ nke a bụ nke a tụọrọ nke a bụ nke a.

levels.label: Sarcastic phrases and rhetorical questions
levels.translation: Okwu ndoro ndoro na nkọwa ndoro ndoro

examples.original: Oh, great. Another meeting on Monday morning.
examples.phonetic: /oʊ, ɡreɪt. əˈnʌðər ˈmiːtɪŋ ɒn ˈmʌndeɪ ˈmɔːrnɪŋ/
examples.translation: Oh, mma! Ọzọ, ụgbọ mmiri nꞌizugbe nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a.
examples.note: Nkọwa ndoro ndoro na-akwado na 'mma' na ntughari ndoro ndoro. Ma nꞌime ndoro ndoro, ọ bụ mma.

examples.original: Do you mind? I'm trying to work here.
examples.phonetic: /duː juː maɪnd? aɪm ˈtraɪɪŋ tə wɜːrk hɪər/
examples.translation: Ị na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a? Am a na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a.
examples.note: Nkọwa ndoro ndoro tụọrọ nke a bụ nke a tụọrọ nke a bụ nke a, tụọrọ nke a bụ nke a tụọrọ nke a.

examples.original: Well, that's just perfect. My car broke down again.
examples.phonetic: /wɛl, ðæts dʒʌst pərˈfɛkt. maɪ kɑːr broʊk daʊn əˈɡen/
examples.translation: Nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a! Ọ bụrụ na m nwere ike ịmalite ịnweta ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Uso sarcástico de 'perfect' para indicar lo contrario.

levels.label: Euphemisms for sensitive topics
levels.translation: Eufemisms tụọrọ ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro

examples.original: He's between jobs at the moment.
examples.phonetic: /hiːz bɪˈtwiːn dʒɑːbz æt ðə ˈmoʊmənt/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a n'okwu ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Eufemism ndoro ndoro tụọrọ 'were unemployed' nꞌime ndoro ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: She's had some cosmetic adjustments.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiːz hæd sʌm kɒzˈmɛtɪk əˈdʒʌstmənts/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a n'okwu ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Eufemism tụọrọ nke a bụ nke a tụọrọ nke a bụ nke a.

examples.original: He passed away peacefully in his sleep.
examples.phonetic: /hiː pæst əˈweɪ ˈpiːsfəli ɪn hɪz sliːp/
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ na-eme nnyocha nke a bụ nke a bụ nke a n'okwu ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: 'Passed away' bụ eufemism ndoro ndoro tụọrọ 'were'.

examples.original: We had to let go of a few employees last quarter.
examples.phonetic: /wiː hæd tə lɛt ɡoʊ əv ə fjuː ɪmˈplɔɪiːz læst ˈkwɔːrtər/
examples.translation: Anyị were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were
examples.note: 'Let go' suaviza el despido, especialmente en contextos corporativos.
